extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy and aesthetics; artists/readers interested in Kantian theory of art
extracted.subtask_short: aesthetic judgement and production of art
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts normative criteria Kant gives for judging beauty and for producing beautiful art (distinctions between taste and genius, faculties required, permissible subjects, classifications of the arts, and related anti-patterns). Useful for evaluating or producing works according to Kantian aesthetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste for judging; Genius for producing
rubrics_metrics.description: For judging of beautiful objects as such, taste is requisite; but for beautiful art, i.e. for the production of such objects, genius is requisite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taste is the faculty of judgement required to evaluate beauty; genius is the special productive talent needed to create works of beautiful art. Distinguish evaluative competence (taste) from creative talent (genius) when assessing works or creators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural beauty judged without concept/purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to judge a natural beauty as such I need not have beforehand a concept of what sort of thing the object is to be; its mere form pleases by itself in the act of judging it without any knowledge of the purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating natural beauty, do not require reference to a purpose or function; focus on the form as it presents itself to judgement. If purposiveness is inferred, the judgement is no longer purely aesthetical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial beauty requires a concept of the product's purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: If the object is given as a product of art, and as such is to be declared beautiful, because art always supposes a purpose in the cause, there must be at bottom in the first instance a concept of what the thing is to be; the perfection of the thing must be taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging art (artificial beauty), evaluate how well the work conforms to a concept of its intended purpose and the perfection of that realization; aesthetic judgement must consider purposiveness in art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art may represent ugliness but not disgust
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful art can describe as beautiful things which may be in nature ugly or displeasing (e.g., the Furies, diseases); but that one kind of ugliness which cannot be represented without destroying aesthetical satisfaction is that which excites disgust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic depiction of ugly or calamitous subjects can still be beautiful unless the representation provokes disgust — a sensation where the object intrudes upon enjoyment and precludes aesthetic appreciation. Avoid representations that make the aesthetic and the object's repulsiveness indistinguishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of allegory/attribute for repulsive themes (esp. sculpture)
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of sculpture, because in its products art is almost interchangeable with nature, excludes from its creations the immediate representation of ugly objects; it represents death by a beautiful genius, the warlike spirit by Mars, and permits such things to be represented only by an allegory or attribute that has a pleasing effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representing calamitous or repulsive themes in media that closely mimic nature, employ allegory, attributes, or indirect means so as not to destroy aesthetic satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste is a judging, not a productive faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Taste, after he has exercised and corrected it by manifold examples from art or nature, checks his work; taste is merely a judging and not a productive faculty; what is appropriate to it is not therefore a work of beautiful art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that technical skill or learned rules alone (taste cultivated by examples) may produce pleasing form but do not make the producer a genius; distinguishing tasteful production from genuinely beautiful art is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful form as vehicle of communication distinct from art proper
rubrics_metrics.description: A pleasing form that is given to a product may be the vehicle of communication (e.g., table appointments, a moral treatise, even a sermon) and yet not be called a work of beautiful art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether form merely serves clarity or function versus whether it accomplishes the free, purposive play of faculties that characterizes beautiful art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius defined by production of aesthetical Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius is the faculty of presenting aesthetical Ideas: representations of the Imagination which occasion much thought without any definite concept being adequate to them; genius finds Ideas for a given concept and the expression that communicates the subjective state universally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate creative works by whether they present 'aesthetical Ideas'—images or attributes that extend imagination beyond determinate concepts and elicit rich, inexpressible thought—rather than merely applying known rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetical Ideas quicken thought without definite concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: An aesthetical Idea is that representation of the Imagination which occasions much thought, without, however, any definite thought, i.e. any concept, being capable of being adequate to it; it cannot be completely encompassed and made intelligible by language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that generate associative, expansive thought and cannot be fully captured in concepts exemplify aesthetic Idea; judge art partly by its capacity to evoke such open-ended associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius as free-but-purposive interplay of Imagination and Understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius properly consists in the happy relation between Imagination and Understanding, which no science can teach and no industry can learn, by which Ideas are found for a given concept; the Imagination is free yet purposive in reference to the presentment of the concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether imaginative originality remains in a purposive relation to understanding (form and intelligibility) rather than descending into lawless novelty or mere rule-following.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression (spirit) required to make the ineffable communicable
rubrics_metrics.description: To express the ineffable element in the state of mind implied by a certain representation and to make it universally communicable requires a faculty of seizing the quickly passing play of Imagination and unifying it in a concept that can be communicated without constraint of rules—this is 'spirit'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge not only the presence of imaginative Ideas but also the artist's power to express and communicate the accompanying subjective state (spirit); lack of communicative expression weakens genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius must be original and exemplary, not imitable
rubrics_metrics.description: The product of a genius is an example, not to be imitated (for then that which in it is genius would be lost), but to be followed by another genius; imitation that copies deformities or singularities becomes mere aping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish exemplary originality (which may inspire but should not be slavishly copied) from mannerism or aping; penalize works that imitate surface peculiarities without the underlying talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner (modus aestheticus) vs Method (modus logicus)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two ways to put together notions of expression: 'manner' (has feeling of unity in presentment) and 'method' (follows definite principles); the former alone avails for beautiful art. Mannerism is a fault when exposition is founded on singularity and not made appropriate to the Idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer works showing an organic, feeling-based unity (manner) over those strictly following rules (method); beware mannerism where peculiar style substitutes for appropriate expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ostentation and affected singularity (aping/mannerism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ostentatious, contorted, and affected manner adopted to differentiate oneself from ordinary persons betrays a bungler; mannerism separates oneself by peculiarity without possessing exemplary talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat exaggerated self-differentiation and affected gestures as faults; authentic originality should serve the Idea, not self-display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste disciplines and polishes genius; balance required
rubrics_metrics.description: Taste, like Judgement in general, is the discipline (training) of Genius; it clips its wings, makes it cultured and polished, and gives guidance as to where and how far it may extend itself if it is to remain purposive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating works, value the shaping influence of taste that brings clarity, order, and universal communicability to imaginative abundance; unbridled imagination may be nonsense if unchecked by judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: If conflict, Judgement should not permit prejudice to Understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: If in the conflict of Imagination and Judgement something must be sacrificed, it should be rather on the side of genius; the Judgement will rather sacrifice the freedom and wealth of the Imagination than permit anything prejudicial to the Understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize conformity to intelligible principles (Understanding) over unchecked imaginative excess when a work threatens coherence or communicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful art must appear free and avoid studied anxiety
rubrics_metrics.description: All that is studied and anxious must be avoided in beautiful art; it must be free art in a double sense and not a work like that of a tradesman whose magnitude can be judged, exacted, or paid for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate apparent spontaneity and freedom of play in works; overly calculated or 'commercial' appearance diminishes the status of a work as beautiful art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential element of beautiful art is purposive form (not mere sensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: In all beautiful art the essential thing is the form, which is purposive as regards our observation and judgement, where the pleasure is at the same time cultivation and disposes the spirit to Ideas; the essential element is not the matter of sensation (charm or emotion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize formal purposiveness that cultivates the mind; mere sensory charm or emotional arousal without idea-communicative form leads to transient enjoyment and eventual distaste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination with moral Ideas secures self-sufficing satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the beautiful arts are brought into combination with moral Ideas, which alone bring with them a self-sufficing satisfaction, they avoid becoming mere distraction that renders the mind more discontented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that integrate moral or intellectual depth provide enduring satisfaction; evaluate whether an artwork connects to moral Ideas rather than merely entertaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of arts by mode of expression (word, deportment, tone)
rubrics_metrics.description: A convenient division of the beautiful arts is by analogy with modes of expression in speech: word (arts of speech), deportment (formative arts), and tone (play of sensations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the tri-partite classification to apply appropriate evaluative standards to different arts: rhetoric/poetry (speech), sculpture/painting/architecture (formative arts), music/color (play of sensations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetoric vs Poetry: honesty and promise/fulfilment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetoric is the art of carrying on a serious business of the Understanding as if it were a free play of the Imagination; poetry is the art of conducting a free play of the Imagination as if it were a serious business of the Understanding. Poetry declares itself play and thereby is more honest and enriching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge rhetoric critically for potential deception (especially in law/pulpit); prize poetry for its candid play that nevertheless enriches understanding. Evaluate whether a speech or text keeps or subverts its promise to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formative arts: plastic (sensible truth) vs painting (sensible illusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formative arts are either arts of sensible truth (Plastic: sculpture and architecture) or of sensible illusion (Painting). Plastic presents corporeal concepts as if they might exist in nature; architecture is for use and thus limits aesthetic Ideas; painting gives illusory appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply different standards: sculpture/architecture assessed for bodily presentation and (for architecture) utility/purpose; painting assessed for pictorial arrangement and illusory representation. Note how purpose/use limits aesthetic latitude (esp. architecture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Art of play of sensations (music and color): judgement via proportion and intelligible differences
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of the beautiful play of sensations (hearing and sight) concerns proportion (tone); judging music may rely on a mathematical element enabling us to pronounce on proportions; presence of intelligible distinctions fixes the ground for aesthetic judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating music or color-based arts, consider whether there are perceivable proportional relations or intelligible structural elements that allow judgement beyond mere pleasantness; absence of such elements may make a work only 'pleasant' rather than 'beautiful'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining arts increases artistry but not necessarily beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Combinations (e.g., poetry with music and theater in opera) can make art more artistic but may not make it more beautiful because so many different kinds of satisfaction can cross one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate multi-modal works both for their internal unity of form and for whether combined satisfactions conflict or dilute aesthetic purposiveness; beware of cross-satisfaction diminishing lasting aesthetic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative aesthetic worth and caution about rhetoric's persuasive art
rubrics_metrics.description: Of all the arts poetry maintains the first rank (originating in genius), while rhetoric as the art of persuasion borrows from poetry and can be objectionable in law or pulpit because it may deprive the audience of freedom of judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank works with attention to their aims: prize poetic art for its imaginative honesty; treat persuasive art (rhetoric) with suspicion when it aims to sway before judgement is formed, especially in morally weighty contexts.
